bull_bear.body: Parent committed up to $100M total ($30M deployed); new raise is structured debt (INR 200 Cr) + equity (INR 100 Cr) to preserve parent balance sheet and avoid dilution. Future funding contingent on opportunity set.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on 2-3 year product commercialization cycles; rapid obsolescence in AI chip architectures; integration risks with Kinetic Technologies; dependency on foundry partners (TSMC/GlobalFoundries) for supply.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly aggressive and visionary; emphasizing 'once in a generation' opportunity, disciplined capital efficiency, and strategic separation from parent to unlock value.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The financing structure is primarily debt (2:1 debt-to-equity ratio) to avoid early equity dilution despite high growth, signaling confidence in cash flow generation from Kinetic assets; the unit is explicitly being groomed for a potential future spin-off.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Completed the buyback: "Completed the extinguishment of 6.4 million equity shares of Cyient Limited, bought back at a price of INR 1,125 per equity share for an aggregate consideration of INR 720 crores (representing roughly 5.76% of the company's total paid-up capital)", executed through the tender offer route.
- "The Promoter group, Directors and KMP did not participate in the buyback", which the MD frames as "reinforcing their continued confidence in the long-term value of the company".
- DET remains net cash: cash and cash equivalents including treasury investments of Rs 16,553 Mn against total debt of Rs 116 Mn (all short-term; long-term borrowings nil), giving net cash of Rs 16,437 Mn versus Rs 14,838 Mn in Q4 FY26.
- Group long-term borrowings rose sharply to Rs 7,668 Mn from Rs 778 Mn in Q4 FY26 and Rs 939 Mn in Q1 FY26, while group cash and cash equivalents fell to Rs 11,877 Mn from Rs 15,063 Mn.
- Cash conversion is disclosed at DET level: FCF of Rs 1,137 Mn with "FCF to Normalised PAT conversion" of 80.5% (163.1% in Q4 FY26, 69.5% in Q1 FY26); the MD points to "a strengthened balance sheet" and "balance-sheet discipline".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Diversified, complementary business portfolio across DET (engineering services), DLM (engineering-led manufacturing) and Semiconductors (IP-led silicon), giving resilience in volatile markets
- Strong global delivery capabilities and operational resilience
- Deep domain expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and digital technologies
- Long-standing customer relationships built on trust and domain expertise, with renewed partnerships during the year
- Global footprint with 15,000+ employees ("Cyientists") across 22 countries
- Debt-free balance sheet with adequate liquidity (₹11,759 Mn liquid assets as at 31 March 2026) supporting operational and strategic priorities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data security and client IP leakage — BRSR material-issues table lists 'Data Security & Privacy' as a Risk with negative financial implication: breaches expose the company to legal liabilities, financial penalties and customer attrition. Cyient runs a Data Leak Prevention (DLP) solution explicitly to safeguard 'the intellectual property of both our clients and our organization', and the Risk Management Committee separately 'evaluates the effectiveness of the Company's cyber security framework'. For an engineering-services firm holding customer design IP, a single breach is a client-loss event, not just a fine.
- Systemic cloud / third-party platform dependency — BRSR risk row 10, 'Systemic Risk Management': the rise of cloud computing and SaaS introduces server downtime, programming errors and cyber threats that can disrupt critical industries like finance and utilities, which rely on centralised cloud data centres; shifting data storage to third-party providers also raises compliance obligations. Rated a Risk with negative implications. (The disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the source text at 'requires strict ad'.)
- Supply-chain and vendor compliance exposure — BRSR risk row 3: supplier failure on environmental standards raises Cyient's Scope 3 emissions, and 'any instances of regulatory non-compliance by suppliers may expose Cyient to legal liabilities, operational disruptions, and reputational damage'. Mitigated only through a Vendor Code of Conduct, a Sustainable Supplier Assessment Framework and recurring Vendor Meets, i.e. oversight rather than control. Material because the group now includes Cyient DLM manufacturing and an early-stage semiconductor business with real physical supply chains.
- Business ethics / regulatory and reputational liability — BRSR risk row 8: unethical conduct can bring 'serious legal and regulatory repercussions, including fines, sanctions, and operational conflicts', eroding customer loyalty, market share and investor confidence. The Risk Management Committee charter likewise carries legal, regulatory and reputational risk. For a company delivering into aerospace, defence and utilities customers across jurisdictions, a compliance failure can gate client access, not just cost a penalty.
- Talent dependency, retraining burden and workforce well-being — BRSR flags a 'talent shortage in the Software & IT Services industry' (row 4) and rates Occupational Health & Safety a Risk (row 5) citing ergonomic strain, prolonged screen exposure, mental stress and burnout leading to 'reduced productivity, absenteeism, and employee disengagement'. The Chairman states the pace of technological change demands continuous learning and that significant emphasis was placed on retraining and upskilling for AI. Against this, FY26 pay moved backwards: 11,417 permanent employees, median employee remuneration change reported as (5.44%) and the average change for non-managerial salaries as (5.40%), i.e. declines - a retention risk in a skills-scarce market.
- Volatile demand and unproven DET turnaround / portfolio reshaping — Management's own framing: FY26 was spent 'stabilizing our core business amid a volatile demand environment', with a 'structured transformation journey' in Digital Engineering and Technology (DET) showing only 'early signs of progress' and requiring sustained effort. Consulting, described as strategically important, 'has yet to fully realize its potential'; Cyient Semiconductors is 'at an early stage'; and the company is 'taking pragmatic decisions to consolidate or exit areas'. The Chairman concedes macroeconomic and industry uncertainties may persist. Execution of the DET reset, not end-market demand alone, is what the earnings depend on.
- Key-account concentration and relationship-led revenue — The company's stated resilience comes from a narrow set of relationships rather than breadth: the Chairman describes deepening engagements 'with key accounts' and renewing partnerships with 'several of our long-standing customers', calling these 'a critical source of resilience and growth'. BRSR row 6 (Customer Relations) frames the same dependency positively - loyalty drives repeat business and long-term revenue. Cyient DLM's support is likewise attributed to 'strong customer connections and a healthy order book'. The AR text supplied discloses no client-concentration percentage, so the exposure is stated qualitatively only.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Power ASSP (incl. Kinetic) comprises 50-60% of current business; remainder split between Design Services and Custom ASIC Turnkey. ASSP share expected to grow significantly over next 3-4 years as 2-3 year R&D cycles commercialize.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Cyient is a global lifecycle engineering company powering mission-critical industries from design to aftermarket across products, plants, and networks", with 300+ customers and 15,000+ associates across 30+ countries, combining human expertise, deep domain knowledge and AI.
- Group is structured into four segments - Cyient DET, Cyient DLM, Cyient Semiconductors and Cyient Others; DET itself runs three business units: Transportation & Mobility (Aerospace + Rail + Automotive), Networks & Infrastructure (Connectivity + Utilities) and Strategic Units (Mining & Minerals + Energy + Healthcare & Lifesciences).
- Large-deal engine is called out as the growth lever: 5 large deals won in Q1 FY27 in DET and, per the CEO, "the highest pipeline in last 12 quarters".
- Moat is framed as domain-anchored AI: "We have always believed AI is only worth something when the people shaping it truly understand the domain", with lifecycle engineering capability described as opening "a far larger market for us".
- Deck frames the growth engine as resilient - "a diversified revenue mix across our target sectors, as key leadership hires in sales & strategy strengthen our go-to-market engine".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Announced an agreement to acquire TAO Digital Solutions, described by the CEO as "the first step" in delivering on the company's M&A strategy.
- [Funding] Secured strategic financing from EAAA India Alternatives Ltd: $30 Mn of capital (debt and equity) at a post-money valuation of approximately $500 Mn for the power-semiconductor platform.
- [Order book conflict] The group update slide states "We reported our highest-ever order book this quarter and a Book to Bill Ratio of 1.5X", while the MD's message attributes the highest-ever order book and robust book-to-bill to Cyient DLM specifically; both framings are recorded as stated. Separately, DET (excl. Semiconductors) order intake was US$168.2 Mn, up 5.3% YoY, with the deck cautioning that order intake is the total value of all orders received in the period and "some of these orders are multi year and can be executed over more than 12 months".
- [Segment divergence] Cyient DET revenue de-grew 0.5% QoQ and 0.9% YoY in constant currency; within DET, Transportation & Mobility was $72.7 Mn (+14.8% YoY cc) and Networks & Infrastructure $53.1 Mn (+2.5% YoY cc), while Strategic Units fell to $36.1 Mn (-26.2% YoY cc). The MD separately notes Cyient Semiconductors' core business marked its 5th consecutive quarter of organic growth above 5% QoQ.
- [Leadership] Leadership team is Krishna Bodanapu (Executive Vice-Chairman & MD), Sukamal Banerjee (Executive Director & CEO) and Shrinivas Kulkarni (CFO); new senior hires include Rahul Sarkar as Global Head, Alliances & Partnerships and Basker Nagarajan as SVP & Global Head, Avionics Delivery.

It leverages deep domain expertise in engineering, manufacturing, and digital technologies (AI, Generative AI, data analytics, cloud, intelligent automation) to develop and support next-generation solutions for customers.

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Acceleration expected in FY27 via Kinetic integration and ASSP ramp. Margin: Gross margin expansion toward 50-60% mix shift over 3-4 years. Order Inflow: Focusing on industrial/medical ASICs and AI power ASSPs. Capex/Commissioning: Funds allocated to R&D, lab infrastructure, and working capital; no fab capex (fabless).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: $100M qualified pipeline split between Industrial and Medical ASICs; L1 bid on government-backed SCL semiconductor modernization initiative; 7 new GaN products launched with Navitas.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scaling AI data center power solutions (800V architecture); expanding GaN portfolio beyond consumer chargers to industrial/high-density supplies; potential future spin-off/IPO of Cyient Semiconductors as standalone entity.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- "Embracing Intelligence": building intelligence from domain expertise up rather than from models down — layering AI and digital capabilities on deep domain expertise; formally became the company's operating system in FY26
- DET positioned around "Intelligent Engineering" — delivering value across the lifecycle of products, plants and networks, from early design trade-offs to modernization choices made across decades
- Strengthening and scaling the consulting capability as a key focus area in the coming years, viewed as a critical enabler to engage earlier in the customer decision cycle and drive higher-value engagements
- Disciplined execution, strengthening the core business, investing in future capabilities, and creating differentiated value for customers, while maintaining financial prudence and improving operational efficiency
- Capital allocation guided by returning value to shareholders today while retaining capital to invest in growth (e.g., Cyient Semiconductors) tomorrow
- Deliberate investment in building the next layer of leadership depth across DET, DLM and Semiconductors
- Sharpening the portfolio by identifying growth markets to scale meaningfully, while consolidating or exiting areas that do not align with long-term strategic priorities
- Growth built on three complementary vectors — Cyient DET (engineering services and technology-led transformation), Cyient DLM (engineering-led manufacturing), and Cyient Semiconductors (IP-led, AI-driven silicon innovation) — providing a diversified, synergistic platform for growth and resilience in volatile markets
- FY26 strategy anchored around three pillars: Market Impact, Tech Adoption, and Organizational Effectiveness
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Cyient's growth investment is largely capability/platform-led rather than physical-plant capex. It has built the Engineering Intelligence Platform (EIP), a proprietary seven-layer technology architecture underpinning its Intelligent Engineering Solutions portfolio, and a suite of reusable accelerators (CyFAST, CyCHAT, CARE, CyMedge, CyText, CyVision, MADE) to speed lifecycle-solution deployment across industries. In Transportation & Aviation, the FY27 strategy is anchored in scaling AI-led engineering accelerators, deepening Build-to-Specification (B2S) and aftermarket franchises, expanding into sustainable propulsion and digital rail signaling, and capturing a larger share of the indigenous defense- and rail-modernization pipeline, supported by security-cleared facilities. In Networks & Infrastructure, the company is investing in digital twins, AI-led simulations, geospatial analytics, data management, and intelligent operations to support 'Intelligent Network Modernization' for telecom and utility customers. In Energy, the company is deliberately broadening its geographic pipeline (North America, India, wider Asia) and developing new annuity-style offerings to reduce project-led revenue lumpiness.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global engineering and technology services landscape continues to be reshaped by three forces: the rise of Generative and Agentic AI, the realignment of global supply chains, and a growing sovereign focus on critical technologies, semiconductors, defence, and clean energy
- AI disruption is pushing enterprises to consolidate around fewer, deeper engineering partnerships, and demand for domain-led, accountable execution has rarely been higher
- Strategy aligned with key global megatrends including intelligent mobility, sustainability, smart operations, digital healthcare, and advanced connectivity systems
- Key account revenues grew 13%, driven by deeper engagement on what matters most to customers
- The large deal funnel reached the highest level in Cyient's history
- Margin improvement remains a clear priority, with the efficiency program on track to deliver progressive gains toward the medium-term target
- Cyient DLM demonstrated resilience with strong customer connections and a healthy order book, reinforcing its position as a reliable manufacturing partner
- Cyient Semiconductors, though at an early stage, is building foundational capabilities in a strategically important sector, positioning the company to participate in the global semiconductor opportunity over the long term
- DET closed H2 FY26 with positive year-on-year growth in order intake across every business, supported by a strong pipeline that underpins the FY27 outlook
- Order intake grew over 5% in H2 over the prior year's second half
- The large deal funnel reached the highest level in Cyient's history
- Cyient DLM has demonstrated resilience with strong customer connections and a healthy order book
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Cyient Semiconductors has secured INR 300 Cr in structured financing at a INR 4,650 Cr post-money valuation to accelerate its transition from a services-led model to a high-margin IP/Product-led fabless entity. The strategic acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and partnerships with Navitas/GlobalFoundries position the unit to capture the $8.5B power semiconductor market, specifically targeting AI data center power bottlenecks, with breakeven expected by late FY27.

risks.risk: Data security and client IP leakage
risks.note: BRSR material-issues table lists 'Data Security & Privacy' as a Risk with negative financial implication: breaches expose the company to legal liabilities, financial penalties and customer attrition. Cyient runs a Data Leak Prevention (DLP) solution explicitly to safeguard 'the intellectual property of both our clients and our organization', and the Risk Management Committee separately 'evaluates the effectiveness of the Company's cyber security framework'. For an engineering-services firm holding customer design IP, a single breach is a client-loss event, not just a fine.

BRSR risk row 10, 'Systemic Risk Management': the rise of cloud computing and SaaS introduces server downtime, programming errors and cyber threats that can disrupt critical industries like finance and utilities, which rely on centralised cloud data centres; shifting data storage to third-party providers also raises compliance obligations. Rated a Risk with negative implications. (The disclosure is cut off mid-sentence in the source text at 'requires strict ad'.)

BRSR risk row 3: supplier failure on environmental standards raises Cyient's Scope 3 emissions, and 'any instances of regulatory non-compliance by suppliers may expose Cyient to legal liabilities, operational disruptions, and reputational damage'. Mitigated only through a Vendor Code of Conduct, a Sustainable Supplier Assessment Framework and recurring Vendor Meets, i.e. oversight rather than control. Material because the group now includes Cyient DLM manufacturing and an early-stage semiconductor business with real physical supply chains.

risks.risk: Business ethics / regulatory and reputational liability
risks.note: BRSR risk row 8: unethical conduct can bring 'serious legal and regulatory repercussions, including fines, sanctions, and operational conflicts', eroding customer loyalty, market share and investor confidence. The Risk Management Committee charter likewise carries legal, regulatory and reputational risk. For a company delivering into aerospace, defence and utilities customers across jurisdictions, a compliance failure can gate client access, not just cost a penalty.

risks.risk: Talent dependency, retraining burden and workforce well-being
risks.note: BRSR flags a 'talent shortage in the Software & IT Services industry' (row 4) and rates Occupational Health & Safety a Risk (row 5) citing ergonomic strain, prolonged screen exposure, mental stress and burnout leading to 'reduced productivity, absenteeism, and employee disengagement'. The Chairman states the pace of technological change demands continuous learning and that significant emphasis was placed on retraining and upskilling for AI. Against this, FY26 pay moved backwards: 11,417 permanent employees, median employee remuneration change reported as (5.44%) and the average change for non-managerial salaries as (5.40%), i.e. declines - a retention risk in a skills-scarce market.

risks.risk: Volatile demand and unproven DET turnaround / portfolio reshaping
risks.note: Management's own framing: FY26 was spent 'stabilizing our core business amid a volatile demand environment', with a 'structured transformation journey' in Digital Engineering and Technology (DET) showing only 'early signs of progress' and requiring sustained effort. Consulting, described as strategically important, 'has yet to fully realize its potential'; Cyient Semiconductors is 'at an early stage'; and the company is 'taking pragmatic decisions to consolidate or exit areas'. The Chairman concedes macroeconomic and industry uncertainties may persist. Execution of the DET reset, not end-market demand alone, is what the earnings depend on.

The company's stated resilience comes from a narrow set of relationships rather than breadth: the Chairman describes deepening engagements 'with key accounts' and renewing partnerships with 'several of our long-standing customers', calling these 'a critical source of resilience and growth'. BRSR row 6 (Customer Relations) frames the same dependency positively - loyalty drives repeat business and long-term revenue. Cyient DLM's support is likewise attributed to 'strong customer connections and a healthy order book'. The AR text supplied discloses no client-concentration percentage, so the exposure is stated qualitatively only.

one-line thesis: Cyient Semiconductors has secured INR 300 Cr in structured financing at a INR 4,650 Cr post-money valuation to accelerate its transition from a services-led model to a high-margin IP/Product-led fabless entity. The strategic acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and partnerships with Navitas/GlobalFoundries position the unit to capture the $8.5B power semiconductor market, specifically targeting AI data center power bottlenecks, with breakeven expected by late FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Not explicitly disclosed in absolute terms; valuation implies ~INR 650-750 Cr run-rate (6-7x sales). EBITDA/Margin: Currently loss-making due to heavy R&D; target gross margins 50-60% for ASSP segment vs lower for services. PAT: Negative; breakeven targeted late FY27/early FY28. Order Book: ~$100M qualified ASIC/ASSP pipeline; L1 bidder on SCL modernization. Net Debt: Subsidiary carrying ~$100M debt ($80M FX debt for Kinetic + $20M INR debt new raise); Parent cash neutral on this specific raise.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Acceleration expected in FY27 via Kinetic integration and ASSP ramp. Margin: Gross margin expansion toward 50-60% mix shift over 3-4 years. Order Inflow: Focusing on industrial/medical ASICs and AI power ASSPs. Capex/Commissioning: Funds allocated to R&D, lab infrastructure, and working capital; no fab capex (fabless).

one-line thesis: Cyient Semiconductors has secured INR 300 Cr in structured financing at a INR 4,650 Cr post-money valuation to accelerate its transition from a services-led model to a high-margin IP/Product-led fabless entity. The strategic acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and partnerships with Navitas/GlobalFoundries position the unit to capture the $8.5B power semiconductor market, specifically targeting AI data center power bottlenecks, with breakeven expected by late FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Not explicitly disclosed in absolute terms; valuation implies ~INR 650-750 Cr run-rate (6-7x sales). EBITDA/Margin: Currently loss-making due to heavy R&D; target gross margins 50-60% for ASSP segment vs lower for services. PAT: Negative; breakeven targeted late FY27/early FY28. Order Book: ~$100M qualified ASIC/ASSP pipeline; L1 bidder on SCL modernization. Net Debt: Subsidiary carrying ~$100M debt ($80M FX debt for Kinetic + $20M INR debt new raise); Parent cash neutral on this specific raise.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Acceleration expected in FY27 via Kinetic integration and ASSP ramp. Margin: Gross margin expansion toward 50-60% mix shift over 3-4 years. Order Inflow: Focusing on industrial/medical ASICs and AI power ASSPs. Capex/Commissioning: Funds allocated to R&D, lab infrastructure, and working capital; no fab capex (fabless).
order book & pipeline: $100M qualified pipeline split between Industrial and Medical ASICs; L1 bid on government-backed SCL semiconductor modernization initiative; 7 new GaN products launched with Navitas.
segment / subsidiary detail: Power ASSP (incl. Kinetic) comprises 50-60% of current business; remainder split between Design Services and Custom ASIC Turnkey. ASSP share expected to grow significantly over next 3-4 years as 2-3 year R&D cycles commercialize.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling AI data center power solutions (800V architecture); expanding GaN portfolio beyond consumer chargers to industrial/high-density supplies; potential future spin-off/IPO of Cyient Semiconductors as standalone entity.
margins & cost dynamics: ASSP products command 50-60% gross margins (IP-driven); Custom ASIC Turnkey offers mid-tier margins; Design Services offers lowest margins. Cost base heavily weighted toward R&D and talent acquisition.
capex / expansion: Capital raise (INR 300 Cr) directed entirely to OPEX-intensive R&D, lab infrastructure, and working capital; fabless model avoids heavy manufacturing capex.
capital allocation: Parent committed up to $100M total ($30M deployed); new raise is structured debt (INR 200 Cr) + equity (INR 100 Cr) to preserve parent balance sheet and avoid dilution. Future funding contingent on opportunity set.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on 2-3 year product commercialization cycles; rapid obsolescence in AI chip architectures; integration risks with Kinetic Technologies; dependency on foundry partners (TSMC/GlobalFoundries) for supply.
management quality / tone: Highly aggressive and visionary; emphasizing 'once in a generation' opportunity, disciplined capital efficiency, and strategic separation from parent to unlock value.
non-obvious takeaways: The financing structure is primarily debt (2:1 debt-to-equity ratio) to avoid early equity dilution despite high growth, signaling confidence in cash flow generation from Kinetic assets; the unit is explicitly being groomed for a potential future spin-off.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
